newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb blasts Corsican bank as farmers protest.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blasts Corsican bank as farmers protest.

text.p: A bomb exploded at a branch of the Credit Agricole bank in the Corsican town of Polelli before dawn on Tuesday, causing damage but no injuries, police said.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the attack which coincided with eight-day-old protests by indebted farmers on the French Mediterranean island who demand a rescheduling of debts and other state aid.
The farmers' debt to Credit Agricole is estimated at 1.3 billion francs ($260 million).

The protesters have put up roadblocks around the island to block traffic and attempted to intimidate petrol station owners into closing down after they were ejected last Friday from the island's two petrol depots they had occupied.

Prefect (government representative) Bernard Pomel issued a tough statement denouncing the protests as unacceptable. He said authorities had guaranteed fuel supplies to emergency services and would ensure supplies to motorists and school buses.
The island's elected assembly voted overnight a declaration pledging financial help to the farmers.

The head of the executive council, Jean Baggioni, said Corsica, with state help, would pay the farmers' welfare arrears estimated at 460 million francs ($90 million) so that they recover their rights to social security.
In another unclaimed attack, a small bomb slightly damaged a restaurant in Zona, in the south of the island.
Leaders of the Corsican separatist group A Cuncolta Naziunalista decided at a weekend meeting to pursue a violent campaign for increased autonomy from mainland France despite a government crackdown.
The group is the political arm of the Historic Wing of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), which has been battling for two decades for greater autonomy.
